text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and fungal esophagitis, your immune system is severely compromised. Have you missed any doses of your antiretroviral therapy recently, and do you have a current CD4 count or viral load result? REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy shows granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. CD4 Count is 36/mm3.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy reveals multiple discrete, creamy-white lesions in the posterior pole of the right eye, consistent with CMV retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis
